title: 鹧鸪天·醉拍春衫惜旧香
title_en: Partridge Sky: Drunk, I Pat My Spring Robe and Treasure Its Old Scent
author: 晏几道

readings.zh: “天将离恨”的“将”是“拿、用”的意思，读 jiāng。
readings.en: Here the character means to take or use, and is read jiāng.

readings.zh: “许多长”的“长”是长短的长，读 cháng，不读 zhǎng。
readings.en: Here the character means long, so it is read cháng, not zhǎng.

readings.zh: “泪行”是一行一行的眼泪，“行”读 háng，不读 xíng。
readings.en: Here the character means a line, as in lines of tears, so it is read háng, not xíng.

glosses.en: chūn shān: a light robe worn in spring.

glosses.zh: 惜旧香：珍惜衣服上留下的旧日香气，那香气让人想起过去的欢聚。
glosses.en: xī jiù xiāng: to treasure the old scent left on the robe, which brings back happy times.
lí hèn: the pain of parting.

glosses.zh: 疏狂：放纵不拘、不受约束，这里指词人自己。
glosses.en: shū kuáng: free and wild, not bound by rules; here it means the poet himself.
mò shàng: by the road. Mò is a path between fields.

glosses.zh: 渺渺：远得看不清的样子。
glosses.en: miǎo miǎo: so far away it looks faint.

glosses.zh: 茫茫：又宽又远、望不到边的样子。
glosses.en: máng máng: wide and endless, with no edge in sight.
zhēng rén: someone who has gone far away on a journey.
xǔ duō cháng: so very long.

glosses.zh: 无凭语：没有凭据、靠不住的话。
glosses.en: wú píng yǔ: words with nothing behind them, words you cannot rely on.

glosses.zh: 花笺：印着花纹的精美信纸。
glosses.en: huā jiān: fine letter paper printed with flowers.

glosses.zh: 费泪行：白白流下一行行眼泪。
glosses.en: fèi lèi háng: to waste line after line of tears.

translation.zh: 醉中拍着春衫，珍惜上面留下的旧日香气，
translation.en: Drunk, I pat my spring robe and treasure the old scent still on it.

translation.zh: 老天偏用离别的痛苦来折磨我这个疏狂的人。
translation.en: Heaven uses the pain of parting to torment a free and wild man like me.

translation.zh: 年年路边都长出秋天的野草，
translation.en: Year after year, autumn grass grows by the road,

translation.zh: 天天在楼上从早望到夕阳西下。
translation.en: and day after day I wait in the tower until the sun sets.
The clouds are far and faint,

translation.zh: 远行的人回家的路是那么长。
translation.en: and the road home for the one far away is so very long.

translation.zh: 相思本来就是没有凭据的话，
translation.en: Longing is only words, with nothing to hold on to,

translation.zh: 不要再对着信纸白白流泪了。
translation.en: so do not waste more lines of tears on the flowered letter paper.

background.zh: 这首词写离别以后的相思，具体写作时间和写给谁都不清楚。晏几道年轻时常和朋友饮酒听歌，后来家道衰落，朋友离散，那些欢聚的日子再也回不来了。他的词里常常写对旧人旧事的怀念。这首词从一件留着旧香的春衫写起，写年年月月的等待和盼望。
background.en: This lyric is about longing after a parting. We do not know when it was written or for whom. When young, Yan Jidao often drank and listened to songs with friends. Later his family declined, his friends scattered, and those happy days never came back. His lyrics often miss old friends and old times. This one starts from a spring robe that still holds an old scent, and goes on to years and days of waiting and hoping.

author_note.zh: 晏几道（约1038—1110），号小山，晏殊的第七个儿子。他出身富贵，却不会做官，也不肯讨好权贵，晚年生活贫困。他一生重感情，词多写相思和离别，语言清丽，感情真挚。黄庭坚说他有几种“痴”，正是这种痴情成就了他的词。
author_note.en: Yan Jidao (about 1038–1110), also called Xiaoshan, was the seventh son of Yan Shu. He was born rich but was no good at an official career and would not flatter the powerful, so he was poor in later life. He cared deeply about people, and his lyrics are mostly about longing and parting, in clear and sincere words. His friend Huang Tingjian said he was foolish in several ways, and this foolish devotion is what made his lyrics so good.

appreciation.zh: 开头一个小动作很有画面感：喝醉了，拍拍春衫，衣服上还留着旧日的香气，人却已经不在身边。“年年”“日日”两句对得工整，一句写时间一年年过去，一句写人一天天在楼上等，等到夕阳西下。下半首用“云渺渺，水茫茫”两个短句，把眼前拉得又远又空，远行的人回家的路就更显得漫长。最后两句好像是自己劝自己：相思说到底是空话，别再对着信纸流泪了。可越是这样劝，越能看出他放不下。
appreciation.en: The opening gesture paints a clear picture. Drunk, the speaker pats a spring robe. The old scent is still on it, but the person is gone. The two lines with year after year and day after day are a neat pair. One shows the years going by, the other shows someone waiting in the tower each day until sunset. The second half uses two short lines, far-off clouds and endless water, to make the view wide and empty, so the road home for the traveler feels even longer. The last two lines sound like the speaker talking to themselves: longing is only empty words, so stop crying over letters. Yet the more they say it, the more we see they cannot let go.
